note: Issue 4540: `static groupshared uint` lowers to an i1-typed groupshared global. Clause 1 IS the defect: a global in addrspace(3) (groupshared) whose LLVM type is i1, which docs/DXIL.rst:240 says is not a defined memory-access type for groupshared memory. Clauses 2 and 3 are the instrument self-test and anti-vacuity anchor, and they are inside the predicate so reindex re-checks them forever. Clause 2 matches BOTH the broken shape (`addrspace(3) global i1`) and the correct shape (`addrspace(3) global i32`), so it proves the module really was produced and read; if it flips on a release while clause 1 does not, that release is unmeasurable under this predicate, not fixed. Clause 3 proves full DXIL codegen completed -- a compile that failed to parse emits no entry function, so it cannot score as a reproduction. CONTROL (recorded because a predicate with no control is worthless): control-no-static.hlsl is repro.hlsl with the single token `static` removed -- the configuration the issue itself names as correct ("This bug does not reproduce when omitting static"). Run with `run --shader control-no-static.hlsl --label no-static --expect no-match`; measured on main-debug it emits `@"\01?storeTile@@3IA" = external addrspace(3) global i32, align 4` and scores no-match, so clause 1 discriminates rather than matching everything. A second control, control-groupshared-bool.hlsl (`groupshared bool` without static), is also expected no-match and shows the i1 narrowing is not merely 'the variable holds 0 or 1'. match-selftest.json holds clauses 2+3 alone and is bisected linearly beside the primary, so every release has an explicit instrument reading in its own capture. Formatting-drift note: the regexes avoid the `internal unnamed_addr` prefix and the mangled/unmangled name, both of which differ between the two shapes and across releases.
